name: Iapetus from Voyager 2, August 22, 1981, 10:41 UTC
blurb: Saturn's two-toned moon Iapetus, about 1,470 kilometers across. Seen by Voyager 2's narrow-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: The whole of Iapetus, nearly fully lit, from about 1.1 million kilometers away, 4 days before Voyager 2's closest approach to Saturn on August 26, 1981. Its leading side is as dark as coal, while its trailing side is much brighter.

claims.text: about 1,470 kilometers across (JPL: mean radius 734.3 km)
leading hemisphere as dark as coal; trailing hemisphere much brighter
Voyager 2 closest approach to Saturn: August 26, 1981 03:24 UTC
1.1 million kilometers from Iapetus's center when the green frame was taken (OPUS center distance 1,092,138 km)
phase angle 48 degrees (OPUS center phase angle)
